FIRST, the caption identifier. The first printed line of packet page 1 is 'IN-CONVICTION-EXPUNGEMENT-PETITION', set in the same face and size as the document title directly beneath it, at x 60.0-267.8, y 53.0-62.2 on a 612x792 page - above 'VERIFIED PETITION FOR EXPUNGEMENT OF CONVICTION RECORDS'. The same string is the continuation header inside page 2 (y 410.7-420.0). Page 3 opens with 'IN-CONVICTION-EXPUNGEMENT-ORDER' above the order's title. That string is this factory's own document identifier. It is defined as a const at scripts/build-census-v1-in_conviction_<family>-set.mjs:92-93, it is carried as documentId in component-page-manifest.json, and grep finds it in no source record and in no issuer publication - only in this repository's own build scripts and lane artifacts. The builder assigns it to the field literally named formNumber (line 464 for the petition, 501 for the order) and captionBlock() prints it as the first line of the caption. So a document to be filed with an Indiana court carries, in the form-number position, a form number no issuer published. It is also non-discriminating: the identical string prints on all three families, which file under three different statutory sections (I.C. 35-38-9-2, -9-3 and -9-4), so as an identifier it identifies nothing. This is a narrower instance of the same class VF30 withdrew a PASS for at this exact location - DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE 'internal-record-text-printed-on-a-filing', whose recorded standard is 'Filings recite statute citations and rule text only.' FIX03 removed the 'Assigned component identity: <componentId>' line and the builder-facing sentence from the order, and it DISCLOSED keeping the rest: its own return says 'The caption keeps the document identifier and the document title.' So this is a declared retained decision, not a missed repair. I am the first independent reader of it and I disagree with the retention, on the two grounds above. Materially milder. 'Assigned component identity: in_conviction_d6-primary-filing-1' was self-evidently internal; 'IN-CONVICTION-EXPUNGEMENT-PETITION' could be misread by a clerk as a heading rather than a code. It is scored as a defect because of where the builder puts it - the form-number slot - not because of how it reads. captionBlock() is not gated on the fixture, so this is what the route would print at runtime with a real participant's facts. Bounded repair: Drop the documentId argument from captionBlock() in all three builders (scripts/build-census-v1-in_conviction_{d6,felony,misd}-set.mjs, captionBlock at ~line 561, and the continuation-header emitter), so the caption opens with the document title. SEC. 5119(G)'. Do not substitute an invented form number.

SECOND, the source digest on the guidance page. Page 1 of both participant-guidance PDFs prints, for three different components, the same SHA-256 beside three different page counts: '... 2 page(s), SHA-256 b04f2941c91f903e8b8a1718ff4f9bd9120f3744c97354fd810c296f89d041c5', then '... 1 page(s), SHA-256 b04f2941...', then '... 1 page(s), SHA-256 b04f2941...'. It does not: b04f2941... is the digest of a 15-page published bundle from which pages 1-2, 7 and 8 were taken. A reader who tries to verify any of the three by that digest cannot, and the three identical digests beside three different page counts make the claim visibly self-inconsistent on the page. The underlying relationship is honest and is recorded correctly in component-page-manifest.json, which carries a per-page pageIsolatedSha256 for each; it is the delivered guidance that states it in a way that cannot be verified as it reads. Bounded repair: On the guidance page, label the digest as the digest of the published source bundle and state the source page range, or print the component's own pageIsolatedSha256 values instead. ARTIFACTS.finding:
FAIL. The artifact accounting itself is exact and I recomputed all of it: canonical.pdf sha256 8babb053d83bb4fd89e4b58c8f36192c17896f626d06e4138ccbb3e69175eb73 / 1,791,186 bytes / 10 pages, boundary.pdf sha256 5dad12059b4b4802870a2a00eefea94d0cb2894452a971b5182d6c47b73c28ee / 1,791,666 bytes / 10 pages, participant-guidance-canonical.pdf 78fb64ceefe6a97ee088098f34defebcb972d71a58d3f6985b6370f04a36ca15 / 7 pages, participant-guidance-boundary.pdf 8b9d9ddee9f5a29719f461298160ab671d65cc533180514ea7d46f40032fd22b / 7 pages, each equal to what component-page-manifest.json and reports/rendered-artifacts.json declare. What fails is what the artifacts carry on their faces, and there are two distinct things.

FIRST, the caption identifier. The first printed line of packet page 1 is 'IN-CONVICTION-EXPUNGEMENT-PETITION', set in the same face and size as the document title directly beneath it, at x 60.0-267.8, y 53.0-62.2 on a 612x792 page - above 'VERIFIED PETITION FOR EXPUNGEMENT OF CONVICTION RECORDS'. The same string is the continuation header inside page 2 (y 410.7-420.0). Page 3 opens with 'IN-CONVICTION-EXPUNGEMENT-ORDER' above the order's title. That string is this factory's own document identifier. It is defined as a const at scripts/build-census-v1-in_conviction_<family>-set.mjs:92-93, it is carried as documentId in component-page-manifest.json, and grep finds it in no source record and in no issuer publication - only in this repository's own build scripts and lane artifacts. The builder assigns it to the field literally named formNumber (line 464 for the petition, 501 for the order) and captionBlock() prints it as the first line of the caption. So a document to be filed with an Indiana court carries, in the form-number position, a form number no issuer published. It is also non-discriminating: the identical string prints on all three families, which file under three different statutory sections (I.C. 35-38-9-2, -9-3 and -9-4), so as an identifier it identifies nothing. This is a narrower instance of the same class VF30 withdrew a PASS for at this exact location - DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE 'internal-record-text-printed-on-a-filing', whose recorded standard is 'Filings recite statute citations and rule text only.' FIX03 removed the 'Assigned component identity: <componentId>' line and the builder-facing sentence from the order, and it DISCLOSED keeping the rest: its own return says 'The caption keeps the document identifier and the document title.' So this is a declared retained decision, not a missed repair. I am the first independent reader of it and I disagree with the retention, on the two grounds above. Materially milder. 'Assigned component identity: in_conviction_d6-primary-filing-1' was self-evidently internal; 'IN-CONVICTION-EXPUNGEMENT-PETITION' could be misread by a clerk as a heading rather than a code. It is scored as a defect because of where the builder puts it - the form-number slot - not because of how it reads. captionBlock() is not gated on the fixture, so this is what the route would print at runtime with a real participant's facts. Bounded repair: Drop the documentId argument from captionBlock() in all three builders (scripts/build-census-v1-in_conviction_{d6,felony,misd}-set.mjs, captionBlock at ~line 561, and the continuation-header emitter), so the caption opens with the document title. The corpus already contains composed pleadings whose caption opens with the title and carries no slug - data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1/vt/vt-seal-under-25-set--custom-pleading/fixtures/canonical.pdf page 1 begins 'APPLICATION FOR SEALING UNDER 33 V.S.A. SEC. 5119(G)'. Do not substitute an invented form number.

SECOND, the source digest on the guidance page. Page 1 of both participant-guidance PDFs prints, for three different components, the same SHA-256 beside three different page counts: '... 2 page(s), SHA-256 b04f2941c91f903e8b8a1718ff4f9bd9120f3744c97354fd810c296f89d041c5', then '... 1 page(s), SHA-256 b04f2941...', then '... 1 page(s), SHA-256 b04f2941...'. The sentence reads 'Delivered exactly as Indiana Coalition for Court Access published it, N page(s), SHA-256 <digest>', so the digest reads as identifying the N-page document delivered. It does not: b04f2941... is the digest of a 15-page published bundle from which pages 1-2, 7 and 8 were taken. A reader who tries to verify any of the three by that digest cannot, and the three identical digests beside three different page counts make the claim visibly self-inconsistent on the page. The underlying relationship is honest and is recorded correctly in component-page-manifest.json, which carries a per-page pageIsolatedSha256 for each; it is the delivered guidance that states it in a way that cannot be verified as it reads. Bounded repair: On the guidance page, label the digest as the digest of the published source bundle and state the source page range, or print the component's own pageIsolatedSha256 values instead. Assert nothing new; both facts are already in the manifest.
